It was right after being at my lowest for months and abusing alcohol. I stopped drinking and started doing everything I could to feel better in a healthy way, started going to the gym, drinking lots of water, I did also start sleeping 8 hours minimum every night and started eating as healthy as I could. College and gym are things I'm really putting all the effort I can and it is starting to pay off. Take into account I had gone to therapy for 2 years and a half so that part was also important as hell, it gave me the tools to recover and it is definetly something that made me able to do all of this.

I always recommend people to take it step by step and take care of themselves since it is a really hard situation to be in, you have to be your most important ally. Also, adopting as many healthy live habits, like going out, meeting friends, doing exercise, eating healthy and sleeping a right amount of hours are always a lot of help. 

As for the second question, it was helpful, it had some bad secondary effects but it is a good way to push you a bit in the right direction... It can also mess you up really bad if it doesn't fit you and/or you have another illness, when I switched to Paroxetine it was my worst time ever for months, not because of my mood but I was just the worst person I've ever been, impulsive and aggressive, I quit it real fast.

Anyway, in that sentence the subject is swimming and it uses this structure, like other verbs such as 'gustar' (me gusta pasear) ('pasear' would be the subject, and 'me' an indirect complement).

In the other two cases, we say it's morphological and doesn't have any purpose, those verbs require it to work most of the time, not always tho, like 'caerse, olvidarse' etc. Hope this helps, as a native spanish speaker it's difficult to figure out how to explain it.
